Yojan Gautam · October 6, 2026

This presentation summarizes the current implementation documented in the local Terra repository and the thesis materials. It presents an implementation progress report, not completed human-study findings.

Sources: Terra/README.md; Masters-Thesis/docs/ARGOS_CURRENT_SUMMARY.md
The research question

How much local autonomy does
one operator need to supervise
a growing robot fleet?
textPreview: How much local autonomy does | one operator need to supervise | a growing robot fleet?

text:
The study will vary fleet size and autonomy level, then measure
operator workload and mission performance.
textPreview: The study will vary fleet size and autonomy level, then measure | operator workload and mission performance.

text:
The central question concerns scalable human supervision. Candidate fleet sizes in the working summary are 1, 2, 4, 8 and 16, but these are proposed conditions. No comparative human-study result is claimed. The latest implementation has four named modes, which should not be confused with the older conceptual L0–L5 taxonomy.

Sources: Masters-Thesis/docs/ARGOS_CURRENT_SUMMARY.md; Terra/docs/autonomy/README.md

text:
Terra owns local sensing, mapping, planning, control and safety. ARGOS owns operator interaction and fleet supervision. The portable autonomy arbiter runs in both the simulator and the phone adapter. The workspace currently contains 11 Rust crates. ARGOS capability statements come from the Terra acceptance-evidence document, not a fresh inspection of its separate repository.

text:
All four modes use the common authority arbiter. The runtime does not automatically choose an optimal autonomy level. Supervised frontier proposals require approval and revalidation against the latest observed free map. The mode names reflect the current implementation.

text:
TerraPhone supports mode, stop and proposal controls. Remote-supervisor mode sends goals and intent to the simulator, avoiding a second phone waypoint controller for the same rover. Depthless devices hold map-dependent levels. Phone contact sensing is unavailable and must never appear as zero collisions. The optional phone control endpoint is loopback-only. Physical robot capability is not established by simulator or build evidence.

These figures and completed actions are reported by the acceptance-evidence README for a local seed-42 two-rover run through an ARGOS Rust/Zenoh client on port 7448. The JSON evidence is described as residing in the companion ARGOS branch and was not independently rerun for this deck. A component replay and connected control flow do not establish successful operator-study trials. No comparative workload or physical-robot result is claimed.

text:
The seed-based disaster-search world contains broken walls, a chokepoint, rubble and alternate routes. Targets remain hidden until within 5 m and the complete occupancy ray is observed free. Observing rovers must return within 2 m of the origin. These are simulation rules, not a validated survivor detector. Fixed assignment and adaptive switching are separately recorded. Complete-data recording and mission success are separate outcomes. The planned study may use NASA-TLX or a similar workload instrument.

text:
The implementation establishes a platform for experiments. The remaining empirical work includes complete fixed/adaptive trials, subjective workload questionnaires, native device interaction checks and physical validation. The thesis repository holds the outline and Paper 1 introduction/problem-formulation drafts. Papers 2 and 3 remain placeholders. Collaborative mapping, fleet attention scheduling, natural-language commands and phone-local VLA are research directions, not completed capabilities claimed here.
